influences.context: I'm such a big fan of Lorenzi Senni, so of course it had to happen right there and then.

influences.name: DJ HVAD (Hari Shankar Kishore)
influences.context: Having discovered the politically-charged mutations of Hari Shankar Kishore (aka Denmark's DJ HVAD) in her teens, when she was at boarding school, Sonne began honing an electronic palette that prioritized the melodic over the percussive.

influences.name: Da Hool
influences.context: I saw you mention Da Hool in an interview – how did you come across this one? I presume you were talking about "Meet Her at the Love Parade"… "How can you not get across that one haha, I think I've heard it as a child and then Emma (Solid Blake) played it maybe 3 years ago at a Herrensauna party and I was sold, love the track, full on nostalgia and '90's vibes."

influences.name: Emma (Solid Blake)
influences.context: I think I've heard it as a child and then Emma (Solid Blake) played it maybe 3 years ago at a Herrensauna party and I was sold, love the track, full on nostalgia and '90's vibes.

influences.name: Alfredo92
influences.context: My source for dance music is most often my partner Alfredo92 who's a DJ, producer and passionate collector of records. We share the same home and therefore I'm very much exposed to dance music, I actually listen more to dance music than I listen to anything else, more or less willingly.

influences.name: Mariah Carey
influences.context: "Give My All" takes its lyrical cue from Mariah Carey's "My All."

influences.name: Brian Eno
influences.context: When I was around 18, a person I was very much in love with showed me "Music for Airplanes" by Brian Eno. I had never experienced music with that kind of pace and it opened a new world to me.

influences.name: ML Buch
influences.context: I think you reminded me not too long ago, but you were the one suggesting [I should] starting writing songs. [Laughs.] ML: Oh, many years ago. Astrid: Many, many years ago, like 2018. I was like, 'Fuck no. Definitely not.'

influences.name: Tom Jones
influences.context: Hearing Tom Jones in the living room. "Sex Bomb," that kind of stuff.

influences.name: Henning Christiansen
influences.context: Yeah, I guess there's quite a strong avant-garde tradition coming from Denmark, with Henning Christiansen and the Fluxus movement.

influences.name: György Ligeti
influences.context: I'm a big, big Ligeti fan. I feel like he's left a massive impression on me, and I still go back to his work. I was really, really obsessed with his stuff when I was a teenager, but I feel like it comes and goes. He's an incredible composer.

influences.name: Bach
influences.context: And obviously Bach, I've always listened to him, if you're talking about more baroque stuff.

influences.name: Jesper Zeuthen
influences.context: And then I met this iconic jazz saxophonist from Denmark. He's called… oh wow, why can't I remember his name?... Jesper Zeuthen! He basically picked me up and was like "I'm gonna teach you how to improvise, I want you as a part of my band." It was really sweet, we just met up in his flat and played music together, and I started to get a grip of how it is to play an instrument without a piece of sheet music in front of me. I think that was actually quite important for me to get comfortable playing my instrument, and from there on I felt more and more comfortable to get into writing my own music.

influences.name: Eiko Ishibashi
influences.context: I played in Japan, and Eiko Ishibashi was playing before me, but the night before I saw her play with Jim O'Rourke. Then I looked into his stuff and found it through that.

influences.name: Jim O'Rourke
influences.context: the night before I saw her play with Jim O'Rourke. Then I looked into his stuff and found it through that.

influences.name: Aaron Dilloway
influences.context: He's an old influence of mine. I feel like I've been listening to his music from years back.

influences.name: Manuel Troller
influences.context: It was a guitarist named Manuel Troller, who I played with as well in one of my shows. He's made some really amazing stuff as well.

influences.name: Joni Mitchell
influences.context: He was talking about that album… the really famous Joni Mitchell album, with the black and white cover... He said it was his favorite album of all time, and I actually hadn't listened to it before. It was so good listening to it for the first time. She's incredible, and she's taken so many different shifts. It's so great looking through her discography, because she's just trying stuff out. It's really inspiring.
